list.name: board
list.query: SELECT name AS __text, id AS __value FROM boards WHERE id LIKE 'linear:%' ORDER BY name
list.label: Issue board

list.name: grain
list.query: Daily : day, Weekly : week, Monthly : month
list.label: Granularity

list.name: contributor
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '(unattributed)') AS __text, COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '') AS __value FROM whodunit_repos ORDER BY 1
list.label: Contributor

list.name: repo
list.query: SELECT COALESCE(MAX(r.name), LEFT(w.repo_id, 8)) AS __text, w.repo_id AS __value FROM whodunit_commits w LEFT JOIN repo_commits rc ON rc.commit_sha = w.commit_sha LEFT JOIN repos r ON r.id = rc.repo_id GROUP BY w.repo_id ORDER BY __text
list.label: Repository (commit panels)

panels.title: Adoption · $repo
panels.description:
Share of commits in the selected range carrying `status=assisted`.

**Adoption is not coverage.** Coverage beside it counts any valid trailer including `undetermined` — a repository at full coverage may have had no agent involvement at all. Coverage says the instrumentation works; this says the agents are being used.

The delivery dashboard carries the same figure; both follow the time range.

defaults.noValue: No commits in the selected range

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(c.status='assisted')*100.0/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0),1) AS v
FROM whodunit_commits c
JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id
WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
  AND ('${repo:raw}' = '__all__' OR c.repo_id = '${repo:raw}')
  AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000
                         AND $__unixEpochTo()   * 1000000000

panels.title: Acceptance

targets.rawSql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(e.outcome='accepted')/NULLIF(SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')),0),1) v FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.description:
Share of decided tool calls that were accepted.

**The denominator is decided calls only** — accepted, rejected or failed — not all calls. A call whose outcome was never recorded is excluded rather than counted as accepted, which would flatter the rate. See Decided tool calls beside this for the size of that denominator.

A rejection is a human declining; a failure is the tool erroring. Both count as decided, and only acceptance is in the numerator.

panels.title: Median cycle · assisted issues

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE
         WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.lead_time_minutes > 0
  AND $__timeFilter(i.resolution_date)
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
    AND i.issue_key REGEXP CONCAT('^',
        (SELECT SUBSTRING_INDEX(i2.issue_key,'-',1)
           FROM issues i2 JOIN board_issues bi2 ON bi2.issue_id = i2.id
          WHERE bi2.board_id = '$board'
            AND i2.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' LIMIT 1),
        '-[0-9]+$')
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes
HAVING ai = 1) ca) < 10
           OR (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.lead_time_minutes > 0
  AND $__timeFilter(i.resolution_date)
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
    AND i.issue_key REGEXP CONCAT('^',
        (SELECT SUBSTRING_INDEX(i2.issue_key,'-',1)
           FROM issues i2 JOIN board_issues bi2 ON bi2.issue_id = i2.id
          WHERE bi2.board_id = '$board'
            AND i2.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' LIMIT 1),
        '-[0-9]+$')
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes
HAVING ai = 0) cb) < 10
         THEN NULL
         ELSE (SELECT ROUND(AVG(ltm)/60, 1) FROM (
                 SELECT ltm, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ltm) rn, COUNT(*) OVER () cnt
                 FROM (SELECT i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.lead_time_minutes > 0
  AND $__timeFilter(i.resolution_date)
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
    AND i.issue_key REGEXP CONCAT('^',
        (SELECT SUBSTRING_INDEX(i2.issue_key,'-',1)
           FROM issues i2 JOIN board_issues bi2 ON bi2.issue_id = i2.id
          WHERE bi2.board_id = '$board'
            AND i2.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' LIMIT 1),
        '-[0-9]+$')
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes
HAVING ai = 1) c) r
               WHERE rn IN (FLOOR((cnt+1)/2), CEIL((cnt+1)/2)))
       END AS v

panels.description:
**Median hours from issue open to issue close**, for issues whose linked commits carry an AI-attribution trailer.

**The median, not the mean** — half the issues closed faster than this, half slower. Cycle times have a long tail, and the two diverge sharply: measured on this data the mean is 3.47 days against a median of 0.17. The mean describes neither the typical issue nor the slow one, so it is the wrong summary for this shape of distribution.

Read it as a description, not a verdict. Harder work tends to get handed to an agent, so a longer assisted cycle usually reflects **which issues were chosen**, not the agent slowing them down. Nothing here establishes cause.

**How an issue is classified.** Its key is matched against commit messages (`WHO-12` in a commit subject links that commit to that issue). If any linked commit carries `status=assisted`, the issue counts as AI-assisted; otherwise it counts as not. An issue whose key appears in no commit message is in neither cohort — it is absent, not counted as unassisted.

**Scope.** Issues closed within the dashboard time range, on the selected issue board. The Repository filter does not apply: an issue's commits can span repositories, so filtering by one would drop genuinely assisted issues and understate the comparison.

**Withheld below 10 issues either side.** A median over a handful moves hours on one of them, and same-minute tickets — opened and closed in one action — would otherwise set it to zero. Issues with no measurable duration are excluded entirely.

panels.description:
How much **faster** AI-assisted issues closed, as the median of other issues minus the median of assisted ones. Positive is the advantage; negative means assisted issues took longer.

**A difference, not an effect.** The two groups are not randomised — developers choose when to reach for an agent, and tend to reach for it on larger or less familiar work. A gap in either direction may be measuring which issues were handed over rather than what the agent did.

**Meaningless unless both counts beside it are substantial.** With one group at zero there is no comparison at all; with a handful either side, one long-running issue moves this by hours.

**Withheld below 10 issues either side.** A median over a handful moves hours on one of them, and same-minute tickets — opened and closed in one action — would otherwise set it to zero. Issues with no measurable duration are excluded entirely.

panels.title: Commits · assisted / total

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CONCAT(
         FORMAT(SUM(c.status = 'assisted'), 0), ' / ',
         FORMAT(COUNT(*), 0)) AS v
FROM whodunit_commits c
JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id
WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
  AND ('${repo:raw}' = '__all__' OR c.repo_id = '${repo:raw}')
  AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000
                         AND $__unixEpochTo()   * 1000000000

panels.description:
Commits carrying `status=assisted`, against every commit whodunit recorded in the range.

Shown as a pair because the count alone is not a measurement — 166 means nothing without knowing whether the total was 200 or 2,000. The Adoption gauge above is this same ratio as a percentage.

**This counts commits.** The issue panels beside it count issues, and the two are not related — an issue may have many commits or none.

panels.title: Decided calls

panels.description:
How many tool calls have a recorded outcome, and therefore how much the acceptance rate beside this is actually measured on.

Shown because a percentage without its denominator is not a measurement. A rate over a handful of calls moves entirely on one of them.

panels.title: Commits by month · $repo

targets.rawSql:
SELECT IF('$grain'='day',  DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000)),
    IF('$grain'='week', DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000)
                             - INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000)) DAY),
                        DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000)
                             - INTERVAL DAYOFMONTH(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000))-1 DAY))) AS `time`,
       NULLIF(SUM(c.status =  'assisted'), 0) AS `assisted`,
       NULLIF(SUM(c.status <> 'assisted'), 0) AS `not assisted`,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(c.status = 'assisted') / COUNT(*), 0) AS `% assisted`
FROM whodunit_commits c
JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id
WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
  AND ('${repo:raw}' = '__all__' OR c.repo_id = '${repo:raw}')
  AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000
                         AND $__unixEpochTo()   * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time`
ORDER BY `time`

defaults.noValue: No commits in the selected range

panels.description:
The amber line is the **share of commits that were AI-assisted**, on the right axis. Exact values per period are on hover — Grafana's timeseries panel has no per-point labels, and a bar chart that could print them cannot draw the line.

A period still in progress is marked **·** after its label — its bar is lower because the period is not over, not because activity dropped.

Stacked, so bar height is total commit volume and the coloured share is adoption. A period with no assisted commits is a full bar of manual work, not an empty one — zero assisted is a measurement. A period with no commits at all is absent.

Buckets follow the dashboard time range: a short range shows a bar per day, a long one aggregates. Commit volume over this window tracks instrumentation as much as output — commits rose 29 to 418 across four months while instrumented repositories went 1 to 3, so per repository the figure is nearly flat (29, 124, 134.5, 139.3). Read volume alongside the repository count before concluding anything about throughput.

panels.title: Issues opened vs closed · $board

targets.rawSql:
SELECT IF('$grain'='day',  days.d,
    IF('$grain'='week', DATE(days.d - INTERVAL WEEKDAY(days.d) DAY),
                        DATE(days.d - INTERVAL DAYOFMONTH(days.d)-1 DAY))) AS `time`,
       NULLIF(SUM(COALESCE(o.opened, 0)), 0) AS `opened`,
       NULLIF(SUM(COALESCE(c.closed,  0)), 0) AS `closed`
FROM (
  SELECT DATE(i.created_date) d FROM issues i
  JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
  WHERE bi.board_id = '$board' AND i.created_date IS NOT NULL
    AND $__timeFilter(i.created_date)
  UNION
  SELECT DATE(i.resolution_date) FROM issues i
  JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
  WHERE bi.board_id = '$board' AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL
    AND i.status = 'DONE' AND $__timeFilter(i.resolution_date)
) days
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE(i.created_date) d, COUNT(*) opened FROM issues i
  JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
  WHERE bi.board_id = '$board' AND i.created_date IS NOT NULL
    AND $__timeFilter(i.created_date) GROUP BY d
) o ON o.d = days.d
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE(i.resolution_date) d, COUNT(*) closed FROM issues i
  JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
  WHERE bi.board_id = '$board' AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL
    AND i.status = 'DONE' AND $__timeFilter(i.resolution_date) GROUP BY d
) c ON c.d = days.d
GROUP BY `time`
ORDER BY `time`

defaults.noValue: No issues opened or closed on this board in the selected range

panels.description:
Issues opened and closed per period, on the selected board.

**Closed means closed in that period, whatever period it was opened in.** Measured here, 141 of 240 issues over three months — so the bars are not a matched pair and the gap between them is not this period's arithmetic.

Scoped by issue board rather than repository: an issue is reachable from a repository only through its commits, and most issues have none — 109 of 379 here. A repository filter would silently drop the rest.

panels.title: Cycle time trend · $board

targets.rawSql:
SELECT IF('$grain'='day', DATE(i.resolution_date), IF('$grain'='week', DATE(i.resolution_date - INTERVAL WEEKDAY(i.resolution_date) DAY), DATE(i.resolution_date - INTERVAL DAYOFMONTH(i.resolution_date)-1 DAY))) AS `time`,
       ROUND(AVG(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, i.created_date, i.resolution_date) / 60.0), 1)
         AS `avg cycle hours`,
       COUNT(DISTINCT i.id) AS `issues closed`
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.status = 'DONE'
  AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL
  AND i.created_date IS NOT NULL
  AND i.created_date <= i.resolution_date
  AND $__timeFilter(i.resolution_date)
GROUP BY `time`
ORDER BY `time`

defaults.noValue: No issues closed on this board in the selected range

panels.description:
Average time from an issue being opened to being closed, for issues that closed in each period.

An issue counts in the period it **closed**, but its cycle time is measured from when it was **opened** — so an issue opened in March and closed in August contributes its full five months. The dashboard time range filters which closures are counted; it does not truncate how far back their clocks started.

Read it with the issue count beside it: an average over a handful of closures moves several hours on one or two of them. And roughly half the issues here close within an hour of being filed, which is a recording habit rather than a delivery time — where that dominates a period, this measures how tickets are filed more than how work flows.

Not split by AI attribution deliberately. Assisted issues take longer here (72.4h against 62.8h in the one month with both), which almost certainly reflects harder work being handed to an agent rather than the agent slowing anything down — a split would invite a causal reading the data cannot support.

panels.title: Work by purpose · $repo

targets.rawSql:
SELECT c.purpose AS `metric`, COUNT(*) AS `value`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id
WHERE c.status='assisted' AND c.purpose<>'' AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
  AND ('${repo:raw}' = '__all__' OR c.repo_id = '${repo:raw}')
  AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY c.purpose ORDER BY `value` DESC

panels.description:
What kind of work the agent was used for, from Conventional Commit prefixes and path heuristics.

**Purpose is a label, not an observation.** `feature` is reachable only through a literal `feat:` prefix, so a repository not using Conventional Commits will show almost none — which says nothing about the work itself.

panels.title: Acceptance trend

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(e.outcome='accepted')
             /NULLIF(SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')),0),1) AS `accept %`
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id
WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description:
Daily acceptance rate over decided tool calls.

Same denominator rule as the headline figure: only calls with a recorded outcome. A day with few decided calls swings violently, so read the shape over weeks rather than the value on any one day.

panels.title: Issues resolved · $board

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(i.resolution_date) AS `time`,
       SUM(t.ai = 1) AS `AI-assisted`,
       SUM(t.ai = 0) AS `not AI-assisted`
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
    AND i.issue_key REGEXP CONCAT('^',
        (SELECT SUBSTRING_INDEX(i2.issue_key,'-',1)
           FROM issues i2 JOIN board_issues bi2 ON bi2.issue_id = i2.id
          WHERE bi2.board_id = '$board'
            AND i2.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' LIMIT 1),
        '-[0-9]+$')
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) t ON t.issue_key = i.issue_key
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board' AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description:
Issues resolved per day, split by whether any linked commit was assisted.

Requires a connected issue tracker. The split is per issue rather than per commit, so an issue with one assisted commit among ten counts as assisted.

**The Repository filter does not apply here.** This panel is scoped by issue board, and deliberately so: an issue is only reachable from a repository *through its commits*, and most issues have none. Measured on this data, 109 of 379 issues have a linked commit — a repository filter would silently drop the other 270, which includes every open issue and everything closed without code. The number would look precise and be computed from a biased quarter of the population.

panels.title: Edits & lines

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       COUNT(*) AS `agent edits`,
       SUM(e.lines_added) AS `lines added`
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id
WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description:
Recorded agent edits per day, and the lines those edits added.

Edits count tool calls that touched a file; lines count what those calls wrote. The two diverge when the agent makes many small changes or a few large ones, which is the shape worth noticing.

Lines from rejected or failed calls are excluded — text that never reached a file is not authored code.
